trial_title: Confounder-Corrected Quantitative MRI Biomarker of Hepatic Iron Content
brief_summary: The purpose of this multi-site research is to validate a rapid magnetic resonance based confounder-corrected R-2 mapping method as a quantitative imaging biomarker of liver iron concentrations.

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has hemochromatosis, which is characterized by iron overload, as indicated by the transferrin saturation and serum ferritin levels.

eligibility_table.criterion: minimum age: Stanford- 8years , University of Wisconsin - 10 years, John Hopkins follow- 10 years, University of Texas-Southwestern - 18 years
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is 51 years old, which exceeds the minimum age requirement of 18 years for all listed institutions.
There is no information provided regarding any contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging; therefore, it cannot be determined definitively.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any implanted medical devices or metallic foreign bodies that would contraindicate magnetic resonance imaging?
